sections.name: Hell knight
sections.card:
Summary: A tough monster with 500 hit points. It hurls green fireballs from range and claws you when you are close. In Doom 64 it is less pale than the usual Hell knight and looks closer to the baron of Hell.
Weak points: It seldom flinches, so the best weapons are the rocket launcher, plasma gun and super shotgun, and the chaingun or shotgun also do well up close. Stay out of melee: it claws back, and the chainsaw is a poor choice against it.
Tips: Its fireballs travel faster than an imp's or a cacodemon's and do heavy damage, though with enough distance between you they are not hard to sidestep. In Doom 64 Hell knights and barons of Hell can also hurt each other with their missiles, so you can get the two to fight.

sections.name: Baron of Hell
sections.card:
Summary: With 1000 hit points it is among the most resilient monsters, behind only the cyberdemon and the spiderdemon. It claws when you are close and throws fireballs from range. In Doom 64 it is red-orange and throws red projectiles; green belongs to the Hell knight.
Weak points: It seldom flinches and takes very heavy punishment, so go for the rocket launcher, plasma gun or super shotgun. If you can stay far enough away to avoid being hit, the chaingun and shotgun also work, though slowly. Do not melee it: that puts you in claw range.
Tips: With enough room its fireballs are fairly easy to dodge, especially while circle-strafing; in cramped spaces it is far more dangerous because it is hard to move around. In Doom 64 barons and Hell knights can hurt each other and end up fighting.

sections.name: Mancubus
sections.card:
Summary: A slow, wide monster whose arms are huge flamethrowers; it spits fireballs in bursts. The Doom 64 version is much taller, with a metal body harness and a fuel pack on its back, and smaller fireballs that look more like fiery brimstone. It first appears in MAP09: Even Simpler.
Weak points: A mancubus is slow and a large target, so fast-firing weapons kill it easily, and the rocket launcher is probably the best of all. It stops briefly and gives out a battle cry before firing, so even slow weapons such as the super shotgun can stun it and interrupt the attack.
Tips: Stay away when it attacks: close up you can be hit by two fireballs instead of one. Once an attack has begun it fires all three bursts even after you leave its line of sight, unless it is hurt in the middle of firing, and you can use this to set monsters fighting each other. In Doom 64 its fireballs go off in a slightly different direction than in Doom II.

sections.name: Arachnotron
sections.card:
Summary: A cybernetic brain on a large metal spider body. The Doom 64 version has two plasma guns that fire two blue bolts together in spurts of five, and it keeps shooting for as long as it sees you. It first shows up in MAP14: Eye of the Storm, unless you play the secret levels MAP30: The Lair and MAP32: Hectic first, which hold some too.
Weak points: Its pain chance is medium, so quick-firing weapons like the chaingun do well. Leave the chainsaw alone: the arachnotron is so big that the saw does not reliably connect.
Tips: Its plasma bursts are some of the fastest shots in the game and its quick firing can drain your health fast. Keep attacking, strafe in wide side-to-side steps and duck out of its line of fire from time to time, and you will take little damage. In Doom 64 it often wins monster fights even against a baron of Hell, though with little health left.

sections.name: Cacodemon
sections.card:
Summary: A floating monster with a huge grinning mouth that spits balls of lightning and bites. The Doom 64 version is beige brown with one yellow-green eye and two arms with broken chains hanging from them, and it swings those arms as it flies.
Weak points: It is slow and flinches easily, so it is a fairly easy target. The chainsaw can disable it, and repeating weapons like the chaingun and plasma gun push it back so much that it can barely fight.
Tips: Its attacks are easy enough to avoid that, with space, you can fight many at once and take little or no damage. Be ready for cacodemons to come flying from unexpected places once they notice you. On the Nintendo 64 its shots travel faster than on PC, though the cacodemon itself still drifts slowly.

sections.name: Pain elemental
sections.card:
Summary: A floating monster that, instead of a normal shot, spews lost souls at you. The Doom 64 version is dark pink with a green eye and has two mouths where arms would be, so it can spit out two lost souls at once, and it lets out a low, sinister laugh when it sees you.
Weak points: Keep your attention on the pain elemental itself, and deal with its lost souls only after it is dead. Quick-firing weapons such as the chaingun and plasma gun usually keep the lost souls away; the rocket launcher is a poor choice, because it may release a lost soul while your rocket is flying, and the blast can hurt you.
Tips: Standing at point-blank range no longer stops it spawning lost souls, as it did in other versions. In Doom 64 each lost soul that cannot appear, including those it releases as it dies, blows up for damage comparable to an exploding barrel, and two together are about as bad as a rocket hit. It only spawns lost souls when it has a line of sight to you, so hit it hard and then take cover.

sections.name: Cyberdemon
sections.card:
Summary: A huge demon with 4000 hit points whose left arm carries a big rocket launcher. The Doom 64 version has darker skin and is much bigger than the PC one, and its rockets leave smoke trails. Cyberdemons are fairly rare, found mainly in the secret levels or late in the game.
Weak points: The BFG9000 is the best weapon against it, and the plasma gun does fairly well. The rocket launcher also works, but expect a long fight, and the rockets have to hit it directly because it takes no splash damage. Any other weapon, or melee, takes much longer, so avoid them.
Tips: It seldom flinches, so you will have trouble interrupting its attacks. Circle-strafe and dodge every rocket, since a single hit can leave you badly hurt. The Doom 64 cyberdemon's rockets are faster and leave from the launcher itself instead of the middle of its body, so they travel downward and can explode on the floor next to you without any wall nearby. On the Watch Me Die skill level, MAP17: Watch Your Step ends with two cyberdemons and MAP24: No Escape holds three.

sections.name: Lost soul
sections.card:
Summary: A flying flaming skull that rams you with its jaws wide open. The Doom 64 version has black horns and an open skull burning only at the top, and it recovers from an attack much faster than the PC version. Its viciousness puts it among the most dangerous enemies in Doom 64.
Weak points: It is physically weaker than on PC, and one shotgun blast can fell it. Shooting it while it charges stops the charge, and a shot lost soul is helpless until it hits something, which makes the chaingun handy against a crowd.
Tips: Unlike every other monster, it makes no sound when it notices you, so the hiss of its breath as it launches is often your first warning. Rockets are a bad idea against a group: a lost soul can suddenly dart at you and set a rocket off close enough to hurt you. Lost souls usually come in groups rather than alone.

sections.name: Demon and spectre
sections.card:
Summary: Fast monsters that can only attack up close. In Doom 64 the manual calls the demon the bull demon; it looks meaner, with black horns, smaller red eyes, and bigger teeth and claws, and its melee reach is a little longer. A spectre is the same monster, but in Doom 64 an unaware one looks like an opaque demon tinted green and turns see-through when it spots you.
Weak points: They have no ranged attack, so they pose no danger from far away. The super shotgun can kill a demon at close range in one blast, the chaingun works well too, and a shotgun used hit-and-run is effective. A demon cannot attack while the chainsaw is cutting it, and the chainsaw uses no ammo.
Tips: They run fast, often in a zig-zag, so they close the distance quickly and help box you in. Lure them into a tight corridor where they cannot swarm you from every side, and use the chainsaw. Of all monsters, they are generally the easiest to lead into fighting other enemies.

sections.name: Chainsaw
sections.card:
Summary: A melee weapon that cuts up anything within reach and acts roughly like a fist that hits four times as fast. It uses no ammo. The Doom 64 saw has two blades instead of one, "U.A.C." engraved on top, and does about twice the damage of the PC one.
Uses: It works best against demons and spectres, which you can usually kill without taking damage, and fairly well against cacodemons and imps. Because it hits so fast, it stops flinch-prone enemies from retaliating. Against Hell knights and other demons that hit hard and rarely flinch, it does not work.
Tips: Its reach is 65 map units, just over a fist's 64, so you have to be right next to your target. Facing a pack of demons, retreat into a corner and cut them down one at a time. In open areas against several enemies it is a liability, since it kills more slowly than a berserk fist.

sections.name: BFG9000
sections.card:
Summary: The strongest weapon in the game. It shoots big spheres of green plasma, and one shot can kill almost any monster while its damage also spreads over a wide area to hit several targets at once. The Doom 64 version has a darker look and first appears in MAP10: The Bleeding.
Uses: Its damage spreads across a wide area, so it handles groups well. The plasma ball explodes where it hits, and a moment later 40 invisible rays fan out from you in a cone and hit whatever they reach. The rays hurt even cyberdemons, which cannot be hurt by blast damage.
Tips: It does not fire the instant you pull the trigger: in Doom 64 there is a wait of exactly one second before the ball leaves, and the rays follow about half a second after it hits. The rays go in the direction the ball was fired even if you turn, so keep facing your target. A shot takes 40 cells, and a BFG you pick up holds 40.

sections.name: Megasphere
sections.card:
Summary: A gray-brown orb that sets both your health and your armour to 200 percent; the armour is the same as blue armour. In Doom 64 it shows a helmet like the player's instead of a demonic face.
Uses: One pickup tops up both health and armour at once. It also counts toward the items percentage on the end-of-level screen.
Tips: The first one in Doom 64 is in MAP06: Alpha Quadrant, and the game holds nine or ten of them, depending on the skill level.

sections.name: Super shotgun
sections.card:
Summary: A sawed-off, break-open double-barrelled shotgun. It uses two shells per shot and fires 20 pellets per blast, against seven for the normal shotgun, which makes each shot roughly three times as damaging. In Doom 64 it reloads much faster, in 1.53 seconds against 1.77 in Doom II, and it pushes you back a little when fired. It counts among the weapons you cannot do without in Doom 64.
Uses: A well-aimed blast almost always kills two imps, or a single demon or spectre. It lets you hold your own against tough monsters like Hell knights, arachnotrons and mancubi, and it is often a smarter pick than the rocket launcher against them: it is about as powerful, shells are easier to come by than rockets, and a rocket blast at short range can hurt you.
Tips: The pellets spread wide, even up and down, so it is wasteful at long range: switch to the shotgun to snipe, or to deal with a lone enemy in a maze. It uses the same shells as the shotgun.

sections.name: Plasma gun
sections.card:
Summary: A rapid-fire gun that fires bursts of blue plasma and draws on the same energy cells as the BFG9000. The Doom 64 version has a blue electric tube on its top that buzzes without stopping.
Uses: It is devastating against almost any single opponent and works as the game's all-rounder. Firing continuously halts an arachnotron or a mancubus in its tracks and cuts a baron of Hell's speed and attack rate roughly in half.
Tips: In Doom 64 it fires a little slower than on PC, one shot every 0.133 seconds, but there is no pause after you let go of the trigger and the shots travel faster. At long range, targets usually move too much for a stream of shots to land, so fire short controlled bursts instead of holding the trigger down.

sections.name: Berserk pack
sections.card:
Summary: An item that looks like a dark gray medikit. It brings your health up to 100 percent if it was lower and hugely boosts your punch damage. The screen also goes red for a while; in Doom 64 that haze lasts only three seconds.
Uses: It makes your punch ten times stronger, usually until the level ends or you die: strong enough to turn humanoids to pulp, and sometimes to kill a demon in a single blow. Picking it up switches your current weapon to the fist, so you can suddenly find yourself unarmed.
Tips: The extra strength does not run out when the red haze fades, so do not stop punching because the screen has cleared. Use it hit-and-run: run up, punch, then retreat or dodge. A punch does not latch on like the chainsaw, so aim carefully.
